description: Passive joint moments, one row per joint. A measured row gives, for each direction away from neutral, the onset angle (rad) and polynomial stiffness [k0 Nm/rad, k1 Nm/rad^2, k2 Nm/rad^3] of the restoring moment M = -(k0 x + k1 x^2 + k2 x^3) sign-adjusted per side, with x the displacement beyond the onset. Gap rows list where values could come from; no value is used without a verified source. The measured rows are neutral-centred linear stiffness (onset 0): they act over the whole joint range, not only at its end, and are validated only inside valid_range. They do not by themselves model end-range stiffening, so they will not stop a controller from resting on a hard joint limit; an end-range row needs its own source or an explicit, documented extrapolation. Fitted rows (source_curve) are cubic springs fitted per side of the source curve's equilibrium by non-negative least squares over fit.range_rad (scripts/fit_passive_moments.py); onsets are absolute joint angles.

joints.notes: Not added. MyoHand's forearm muscles already supply most of Formica's value through their passive force-length curves, and that contribution depends on posture: 0.22 Nm/rad about pro_sup = 0 in a two-arm MyoHand model at elbow 90 deg (act = ctrl = 0), 0.056 Nm/rad in myoarm_r / myofullbody (myo_personalise measurement). Adding Formica on top would double-count; a pose-independent subtraction would be wrong. Revisit with an end-range source.

The abduction term c*exp(d(theta - theta_max)) is left out: with the averaged coefficients (c = -2.94 +- 8.2, d = -0.18) it gives about -11 N m at the resting adduction, against at most -1.9 N m measured, so the averaged pair is not usable. Flexion beyond rest was not measured, so the row only resists extension. MyoHand's muscles give <= 2.1 N cm passive moment here (at 30-40 deg extension), against up to 150 N cm in the source: no double counting worth subtracting.
joints.where: Table 1 means (n=10), Eq. (2) first term; Sec. 3.1 ranges

source_curve.mapping: Domalain's Mp is the external moment (negative = extension) in Chao et al. TMC coordinates with angles relative to each subject's maxima; the internal moment is -Mp. phi_max (maximal extension, -43.2 +- 16.0 deg) is aligned with MyoHand's cmc_flexion extension limit (+0.70 rad; +q = extension), as the paper prescribes relative-to-maximum use; fit over the measured range of motion (54.9 deg) from that limit.

joints.notes: Barry et al. 2018 likewise used Domalain 2010 for thumb CMC abduction. The flexion term e*exp(f(phi - phi_max)) (e = -71.89, f = -0.55) is left out (single-joint springs): it is below 5 N cm unless the CMC is within ~5 deg of maximal extension. MyoHand's muscles give no passive CMC abduction moment (|M| < 0.1 N cm), so nothing double-counts.
joints.where: Table 1 means (n=10), Eq. (3) without the flexion term; Sec. 3.1 ranges

source_curve.mapping: theta_max (maximal abduction, 7.4 +- 8.5 deg) aligned with MyoHand's cmc_abduction abduction limit (+0.78 rad); fit over the measured abduction-adduction span (7.4 - (-39.9) = 47.3 deg). MyoHand's range reaches 26 deg further into adduction, where the fitted cubic is extrapolated. The adduction side is a single linear spring: a cubic fitted inside the measured span extrapolates to 5.5-6.8 N m at MyoHand's adduction limit (the source exponential to 7.3 N m), the linear one to 1.8 N m, near Domalain's largest measured moment (141.7 +- 43.9 N cm at the subjects' maximal adduction).

joints.notes: Assumption from Barry et al. 2018 (no thumb MCP data exist): Knutson's index-MCP intrinsic curve with MyoHand's thumb sign (+q = extension). MyoHand's thumb muscles add no passive MP moment (|M| < 0.1 N cm over the range), so nothing double-counts.
joints.where: Barry et al. 2018 Sec. 2.1: thumb MCP passive set equal to index MCP

joints.notes: Barry et al. 2018 set the thumb IP equal to the index PIP, but Li 2006 gives only near-equilibrium stiffness about an index-specific equilibrium (52.5-77.9 deg), which does not transfer to the thumb IP; Kamper et al. 2002 PIP curves are needed.

Intrinsic component only (Knutson Eq. 2, Table 1 medians of 8 healthy subjects; units N cm, 1/deg, deg; theta = MCP flexion). The extrinsic component (Eq. 3, wrist dependent) belongs to the extrinsic muscle-tendon units and is not added. Validation: MyoHand's extrinsic index muscles (FDS2, FDP2, EDC2, EIP) give at most 1.2 N cm passive MCP moment over MCP 0-90 deg and wrist -60..60 deg, against Knutson's extrinsic fit of up to 30 N cm (e.g. -30 N cm at MCP 90 deg, wrist flexed 60 deg): the model lacks the extrinsic passive tension (tenodesis), so with the intrinsic curve alone the relaxed MCP settles near its intrinsic equilibrium (~55 deg flexion) instead of ~27 deg (intrinsic + extrinsic at wrist 0). The intrinsic muscles (RI2, LU_RB2, UI_UB2) add no passive moment except an RI2 path discontinuity: its normalised length jumps from 1.19 to 0.98 between MCP 10 and 15 deg and gives -5..-9 N cm (extension) at MCP 0-10 deg, a MyoHand path artefact.

knutson2000_extrinsic.units: N cm, 1/deg, deg; theta_j = B_j * wrist_angle + phi_j (wrist flexion positive)

joints.notes: Not added: Li reports total moments (muscles included) as equilibria and 20-deg stiffness only, and the equilibrium moves ~20 deg with MCP posture (intrinsic-muscle regulation, the paper's finding), which a joint spring cannot represent. Validation: MyoHand's muscles already give ~0.55 N mm/deg at PIP 60-80 deg with MCP 0 (Li: 0.71-0.76) and ~0 with MCP 60 (Li: 0.43-0.49), and no equilibrium in 30-90 deg (passive moment extends throughout: -0.3 at 40, -3.5 N cm at 90 deg), against Li's 52.5-77.9 deg. Kamper et al. 2002 (curves for MCP/PIP/DIP) is needed for a PIP row.
